meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 16: Community, Governance & Security (multi-select)
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: Your company wants to fork the reference SDK and republish parts of the specification in its own docs. Which statements apply? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Non-specification documentation is CC BY 4.0, so reuse requires credit
The specification, not any SDK's behaviour, is the authoritative source of truth
Redistribution requires the Steering Group's written approval
Code and the specification are Apache 2.0, so a commercial fork is permitted with attribution
Forks may not use the name MCP in any form without a trademark licence agreement

questions.explanation: Apache 2.0 covers code and specs, CC BY 4.0 covers the other documentation, and both permit reuse with attribution rather than permission. Where an SDK and the spec disagree, the spec wins.

questions.question: Which statements about MCP's groups and meetings are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The Member and Community Moderator roles are part of the Steering Group
Core Maintainers meet every two weeks, and decisions are recorded transparently
Interest Groups articulate problems; Working Groups produce solutions such as SEPs
Working Group decisions are final and cannot be escalated to Core Maintainers
Maintainers, Core Maintainers and Lead Maintainers form the MCP Steering Group

questions.explanation: The Steering Group is the three maintainer tiers; Member and Community Moderator sit outside it. Interest Groups identify problems and Working Groups build deliverables, and Maintainers escalate to Core Maintainers when needed.
